ACCEPT. The native-guard lifting lemma, the all-orientation donor injection, and the resulting coefficient-one theorem are correct. The virtual-guard construction is also valid for every stated even parameter choice: it is feasible, single-terminal, has exactly one perfect matching, admits no feasible nonempty exchange, and has the claimed receiver charges and original-board counts.The counterfamily establishes precisely the stated obstruction: a virtual-guard local donor need not remain an original endpoint-free donor. Its signed receiver charge is negative, so the half-area inequality holds with the stated strict surplus.1. Native-guard lifting uses the actual bridge property correctlyUse the displayed orientation and write
$$a=(0,0),\quad b=(0,1),\quad c=(1,0),\quad d=(1,1).$$
The accepted decomposition supplies the crucial fact that every original endpoint edge between distinct completed pieces is a bridge of the original endpoint graph.The upper-left corner is originally blankIf  $a$  is an original endpoint, it lies outside  $K$  by the witness hypothesis. The cycle
$$a,\;(-1,0),\;(-1,-1),\;(0,-1),\;a$$
then consists entirely of original endpoints. It contains an edge between  $a$ ’s piece and  $K$ , contradicting that edge’s bridge status.Also,  $a$  cannot be an original selection: it sees the two distinct occupied endpoints  $(-1,0)$  and  $(0,-1)$ . Therefore  $a$  is originally blank.The upper-right corner is not an original endpointSuppose  $b$  is an original endpoint, necessarily outside  $K$ , and put  $x=(0,2)$ .If  $x$  is an endpoint, the cycle
$$(-1,1),\;b,\;x,\;(-1,2),\;(-1,1)$$
contains the cross-piece edge  $(-1,1)b$ . This contradicts its bridge status, regardless of which piece contains  $x$ .If  $x$  is selected, it sees both  $b$  and  $(-1,2)$ , contradicting feasibility. Thus  $x$  is blank. With both  $a$  and  $x$  blank,  $b$  has at most its two remaining occupied neighbors, contradicting single terminality.Hence  $b$  is not an original endpoint. The boundary qualification causes no difficulty; under the displayed witness on a rectangular board,  $x$  is in fact present because  $(-1,2)$  and the tile are present.These upper-corner conclusions do not yet use the native status of  $q$ .The native guard excludes the lower endpointsBecause  $q=(1,-1)$  is an original selection and already sees  $(0,-1)\in K$ , its neighbor  $c=(1,0)$  must be unoccupied.Suppose  $d$  is an endpoint. Since  $b$  is not an endpoint, it could only be blank or selected. Under this supposition it cannot be selected, because it would see both  $d$  and  $(-1,1)$ . Thus  $b$  is blank. The endpoint  $d$  would then have two blank neighbors  $b,c$ , leaving occupied degree at most two—a contradiction.Therefore  $Q$  contains no original endpoint. Its corners  $a,c$  are blank, and its only possible selections are  $b,d$ . They cannot both be selected, since  $b$  already sees  $(-1,1)$ . Consequently,
$$d_Q=2-|T\cap Q|\ge1.$$
This identifies the use of the native hypothesis exactly: it forces  $c$  to be originally blank. The counterfamily later exploits the failure of that step for a virtual guard.2. The donor injection covers all eight orientationsEach oriented witness has a four-point extended run along one full side of  $Q$ . The eight orientations consist of four choices of full side and two choices of the lateral cap.For two witnesses claiming the same physical tile:Equal full sides: their four-point runs coincide, so they share endpoints.Adjacent full sides: their extended runs meet at the common exterior corner, again sharing an endpoint.Opposite full sides: put the first witness in the displayed orientation. The other full run contains  $(2,-1)$ , regardless of its cap orientation. The original selection  $q=(1,-1)$  would see both  $(0,-1)$  and  $(2,-1)$ , contradicting feasibility.The first two cases force the pieces to coincide because distinct completed pieces have disjoint endpoint sets. The third case is impossible.This proves injectivity across distinct completed pieces, including pieces belonging to the same original endpoint component. No assumption about distinct original components enters the argument.3. The coefficient-one conclusion uses the original board correctlyChoose one native witness for each positive completed piece, and let their number be  $b$ . The preceding results give distinct original endpoint-free tiles, each with deficit at least one.All endpoint-free tile deficits are nonnegative, so
$$\begin{aligned}
\sum_K\rho(\widehat K)
&\le \sum_{\rho(\widehat K)>0}\rho(\widehat K)\\
&\le b\\
&\le \sum_{\text{chosen }Q}d_Q\\
&\le D.
\end{aligned}$$
Here  $\widehat K$  denotes the completed pair.Substitution into the accepted identity gives
$$\frac{mn}{2}-|T|-|M|
=D-\sum_K\rho(\widehat K)\ge0.$$
The bookkeeping is correct in three respects:Each chosen donor is endpoint-free in the original configuration.Injection makes the chosen physical tiles distinct.Nonpositive piece charges remain in the signed sum; no completed-board deficit, interface correction, or raw buffer is introduced as additional supply.Thus the geometric hypotheses imply the coefficient-one bound exactly as stated. The proof requires neither a bound on the number of pieces nor a bound on an original component’s total charge.4. The all-parameter construction has exactly the claimed geometryLet  $O$  be the outer endpoint set and  $I$  the inner endpoint set.After translation, the outer endpoints are
$$\{4,5\}\times\{5,\ldots,W+4\},$$

$$\{6,\ldots,H+3\}\times\{W+3,W+4\},$$
together with
$$p=(6,5),\qquad (H+4,W+4).$$
The inner endpoints are
$$\{7,8\}\times\{5,\ldots,w+4\},$$

$$\{9,\ldots,h+6\}\times\{w+3,w+4\},$$
together with
$$(9,5),\qquad (h+7,w+4).$$
These sets are disjoint. Their only connecting edge is
$$p q,\qquad p=(6,5),\quad q=(7,5).$$
Indeed, the bars are separated by the intervening row  $6$ , where the only nearby outer endpoint is  $p$ . The outer leg begins in column  $W+3$ , while inner endpoints reach only column  $w+4$ . The condition  $W-w\ge6$  separates those endpoint regions by at least five columns.Exactly two supports are consumedThe outer selected set has  $H+4$  vertices and includes  $q=(7,5)$ .After relocation, the inner selected set has  $h+4$  vertices. Its isolated supports are
$$p=(6,5),\quad (7,w+5),\quad (9,4),\quad
(10,5),\quad(h+8,w+4),$$
along with the two alternating leg-support families.Exactly  $q$  from the outer selected set and  $p$  from the inner selected set become endpoints. There are no other consumed supports or coincident retained selections. Hence
$$|T|=(H+4)+(h+4)-2=H+h+6.$$
Feasibility and single terminality hold for arbitrary relative heightsOn the right, outer inward supports lie at column  $W+2$ , while all inner occupied data reach at most column  $w+5$ . Their horizontal separation is at least three.On the left, outer support  $(6,4)$  would conflict with the old inner support  $(7,4)$ . That is exactly the site removed by relocation. The nearest retained inner left support is  $(9,4)$ , at distance three from  $(6,4)$ .Thus retained selections acquire no additional occupied neighbors. At  $p,q$ , an occupied selected neighbor becomes an occupied endpoint, preserving occupancy.The standard elbow’s endpoint degrees are at least three: bar vertices have the required strip neighbors or end support, the short tips have their matched neighbor and two supports, and the leg vertices have the required strip neighbors and alternating supports. Relocating the inner top-left support preserves that endpoint’s degree and changes no other inner endpoint degree.The separation argument does not require an ordering between  $H$  and  $h$ .The rectangle contains every occupied vertexFor
$$m=\max(H+8,h+10),\qquad n=W+12,$$
both dimensions are even. The largest occupied row is at most
$$\max(H+5,h+8)<m,$$
and the largest occupied column is  $W+5<n$ . All coordinates are nonnegative.5. The uniqueness order and support relocation are valid for every lengthThe prescribed matching is completeFor one elbow,
$$|P(w,h)|=2w+2(h-2)+2=2w+2h-2.$$
The five prescribed matching families contain
$$\frac w2+\left(\frac w2-1\right)+1
+\frac h2+\left(\frac h2-1\right)
=w+h-1$$
edges. Their endpoints are disjoint and exhaust  $P(w,h)$ .The leaf-forcing order proves uniquenessThe initial short tip  $(2,0)$  has only the endpoint neighbor  $(1,0)$ , so their edge is forced.After removing that pair, consider
$$(j\bmod2,j)\;-\;(j\bmod2,j+1),
\qquad j=0,\ldots,w-2.$$
For even  $j$ , the left endpoint is in the top row. Its lower neighbor and preceding horizontal neighbor have already been removed, and there is no endpoint above it. Only its right neighbor remains.For odd  $j$ , the left endpoint is in the bottom row. Its upper and preceding horizontal neighbors have already been removed. Since  $j\le w-3$ , the vertex immediately below is outside the leg. Again, only its right neighbor remains.After these edges are removed, the remaining bar endpoint  $(1,w-1)$  is a leaf adjacent to  $(2,w-1)$ .The leg then follows the stated alternating recurrence. For even  $r$ ,  $(r,w-2)$  has only  $(r+1,w-2)$  remaining; for odd  $r$ ,  $(r,w-1)$  has only  $(r+1,w-1)$  remaining. The final  $r=h-1$  is odd and pairs with the bottom tip.The number of forced edges is
$$1+(w-1)+1+(h-2)=w+h-1.$$
Thus every endpoint is consumed and every matching edge is forced. This proves uniqueness for all the parameters, including  $w=6,h=4$ .The relocated support preserves the freezing proofIn inner-relative coordinates, the relocation is
$$(0,-1)\longmapsto(-1,0).$$
The old support is used only to freeze  $T_0$ . The new support is still adjacent to  $T_0$ , and it remains distinct from
$$B_0=\operatorname{mate}(L).$$
Since  $L$  is frozen,  $B_0$  cannot be deleted. Thus  $T_0$  still has the two required retained neighbors.All subsequent freezing witnesses are unchanged. The supplied recurrences are consistent with the matching:The descending even- $R$  wave uses  $R_{r+1}=\operatorname{mate}(R_{r+2})$ .The chamber waves use the stated previously frozen partners and stop at the appropriate endpoints.The leg seeds  $A_2,R_3$  and subsequent zigzag use distinct adjacent retained neighbors.At  $h=4$ , the seeds complete the remaining leg without invoking a nonexistent continuation.The completed inner pair is therefore terminal under its unique matching. The completed outer pair is exactly the standard elbow and is terminal as well.These are exactly the two final even-bridge piecesA standard elbow has only its two tip edges as graph bridges. Every other endpoint edge lies on a four-cycle in the two-row bar or the two-column leg, including at the turn. Each tip edge is odd.The new edge  $pq$  separates two even endpoint sets, so it is an even bridge. Attaching the other even-sized elbow preserves the parity of the internal bridges. Thus  $pq$  is the only even bridge of the union.The accepted theorem now gives both:
$$|\operatorname{PM}(O\cup I)|
=|\operatorname{PM}(O)|\,|\operatorname{PM}(I)|=1,$$
and exchange terminality of the union.6. The receiver counts, including the changed inner phase, are exactThe two translations have different physical row phases. Accounting for that difference gives the stated negative inner charge.QuantityCompleted outer elbowCompleted inner elbowEndpoints $2W+2H-2$  $2w+2h-2$ Matching edges $W+H-1$  $w+h-1$ Receiver tiles $W/2+H+1$  $w+h$ Selections in receiver $H+4$  $h+2$ Receiver charge $1$  $1-w$ Outer receiverThe outer offset  $(4,5)$  has the standard phase. The bar meets  $W/2+1$  tiles. The leg contributes  $H-2$  tiles, and the short-tip and bottom-tip tiles contribute one each. Therefore
$$|\mathcal R_O|=\frac W2+H+1.$$
All  $H+4$  supports lie in this receiver, giving
$$\rho(\widehat O)
=(W+H-1)+(H+4)
-2\left(\frac W2+H+1\right)=1.$$
Inner receiverAt offset  $(7,5)$ , the physical row bands in inner-relative coordinates are
$$\{-1,0\},\ \{1,2\},\ \{3,4\},\ldots,\{h-1,h\}.$$
The first two each meet  $w/2+1$  column bands. The remaining  $h/2-1$  each meet the two leg column bands. Hence
$$|\mathcal R_I|
=2\left(\frac w2+1\right)
+2\left(\frac h2-1\right)
=w+h.$$
The receiver selections are exactly the three individually listed supports—north, top-right, and short-tip west—together with  $h/2$  outer-leg supports and  $h/2-1$  inner-leg supports. Thus
$$|T_{\widehat I}\cap\mathcal R_I|
=3+\frac h2+\left(\frac h2-1\right)=h+2.$$
The lower short-tip support is in a far-left tile in row band  $\{3,4\}$ , where the inner endpoints occupy only the far-right leg. The below-bottom-tip support lies in an entirely endpoint-free row band. They are correctly excluded.Therefore
$$\rho(\widehat I)
=(w+h-1)+(h+2)-2(w+h)=1-w.$$
Direct original-board countThe completed receivers overlap only at the bridge tile
$$Q_b=\{6,7\}\times\{4,5\}.$$
Consequently the original receiver has
$$r_{\mathrm{orig}}=\frac W2+H+w+h$$
tiles. Removing the two virtual selections  $p,q$  from the completed receiver-selection counts gives
$$s_{\mathrm{orig}}=H+h+4.$$
The complete original matching count is
$$|M|=W+H+w+h-2.$$
These counts directly verify
$$\begin{aligned}
\rho_{\mathrm{whole}}
&=(W+H+w+h-2)+(H+h+4)\\
&\qquad-2\left(\frac W2+H+w+h\right)\\
&=2-w.
\end{aligned}$$
Thus the charge calculation agrees with the accepted additive identity.Only the two stated inner supports lie outside the original receiver. For the specified blank-exterior construction, the exact original deficit can also be written
$$D=\frac{mn}{2}-W-2H-2w-2h-2.$$
It follows that
$$\frac{mn}{2}-|T|-|M|
=D+w-2\ge w-2\ge4,$$
as claimed.7. The lost donor disproves the transport rule at exactly the claimed pointFor
$$Q=\{6,7\}\times\{6,7\},$$
the outer witness endpoints are
$$(5,5),(5,6),(5,7),(5,8),(6,5),$$
and its completed selected guard is
$$q=(7,5).$$
The completed outer pair contains no endpoint or selection in  $Q$ , so its local deficit is exactly  $2$ .In the original configuration,
$$(7,6),(7,7)\in I.$$
Therefore  $Q$  is an original endpoint-bearing tile and contributes nothing to the original endpoint-free deficit  $D$ .The upper corners remain blank, consistently with the bridge-cycle part of the lifting proof. The obstruction occurs in the lower row:  $q$  is originally an endpoint, so its adjacency to  $p$  does not force  $(7,6)$  blank.This is a counterexample to automatic donor lifting from a virtual-guard certificate, even under uniqueness and full exchange terminality. It supplies no counterexample to the native-guard theorem or to the half-area target. The signed charges are
$$1+(1-w)=2-w<0,$$
and the negative inner charge already accounts for the favorable net balance. The vanished local capacity  $2$  cannot be added to that balance as further original supply.No unresolved gap remains in the new compensation lemma or in the stated all-parameter obstruction.
